learningObjectives.title: Trench warfare and the Western Front

questions.q: Which three countries made up the Triple Alliance of 1882?
questions.explain: The Triple Alliance of 1882 bound Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy together in a defensive agreement.

questions.q: On what date was Archduke Franz Ferdinand assassinated at Sarajevo?
questions.explain: Franz Ferdinand and his wife were shot in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914, sparking the July Crisis.

questions.q: Who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand?
questions.explain: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb linked to the Black Hand group, carried out the assassination.

questions.q: The Entente Cordiale of 1904 was an agreement between which two countries?
questions.explain: The 1904 Entente Cordiale settled colonial disputes and drew Britain and France closer together.

questions.q: At which battle did the Germans first make major use of poison (chlorine) gas on the Western Front?
questions.explain: Chlorine gas was released on a large scale by the Germans at the Second Battle of Ypres in April 1915.

questions.q: On what date did the first day of the Battle of the Somme take place?
questions.explain: The Somme opened on 1 July 1916, the bloodiest single day in British Army history.

questions.q: In which year did the Battle of Verdun take place?
questions.explain: Verdun was fought from February to December 1916 as a German attempt to 'bleed France white'.

questions.q: On what date was the Armistice that ended the fighting signed?
questions.explain: The Armistice came into effect at 11am on 11 November 1918, ending the fighting on the Western Front.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the Schlieffen Plan?
options: To defeat France quickly before turning to fight Russia
To invade Britain across the English Channel
To capture the Balkans from Austria-Hungary
To blockade German ports and starve the population
questions.explain: The plan aimed to knock out France in six weeks, avoiding a prolonged war on two fronts against France and Russia.

questions.q: Why was the Agadir (Second Moroccan) Crisis of 1911 significant for growing tensions in Europe?
options: It increased hostility between Germany and Britain/France and strengthened the Entente
It caused Italy to leave the Triple Alliance
It began the naval race between Britain and Germany
It led directly to the annexation of Bosnia
questions.explain: Germany's gunboat at Agadir alarmed Britain and France, drawing them closer together against Germany.

questions.q: How did the system of alliances help turn a local dispute into a European-wide war in 1914?
options: It meant an attack on one country could draw its allies into the conflict
It forced all countries to disarm and rely on diplomacy
It guaranteed that only Austria-Hungary and Serbia would fight
It ensured Britain would remain neutral in any war
questions.explain: Once Austria attacked Serbia, the alliance obligations pulled Russia, Germany, France and Britain in one after another.

questions.q: Why did a stalemate of trench warfare develop on the Western Front by the end of 1914?
options: Defensive weapons like machine guns and artillery made attacks across no man's land very costly
Both sides had run out of soldiers and ammunition
Bad weather made all fighting impossible until 1918
Neither side had any modern weapons
questions.explain: Machine guns, artillery and barbed wire favoured defenders, so neither side could break through, producing a deadlock.

questions.q: Why was the First Battle of the Marne (September 1914) important?
options: It halted the German advance and ended hopes of a quick victory
It was the first battle in which tanks were used
It forced Russia to leave the war
It marked the entry of the USA into the war
questions.explain: The Allied stand at the Marne stopped the German advance on Paris and wrecked the Schlieffen Plan's timetable.

questions.q: What was the main reason the United States entered the war in April 1917?
options: Germany's renewal of unrestricted submarine warfare against shipping
questions.explain: Unrestricted U-boat attacks on Atlantic shipping, alongside the Zimmermann Telegram, pushed the USA to declare war.

questions.q: How did Russia's exit from the war in early 1918 affect the fighting on the Western Front?
options: It allowed Germany to move troops west for a major offensive
It forced Germany to surrender immediately
It brought Britain and France to the peace table
It ended the naval blockade of Germany
questions.explain: After the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, Germany transferred troops from the east to launch its Spring Offensive in the west.

questions.q: What was the main aim of the German Ludendorff (Spring) Offensive of March 1918?
options: To win the war before large numbers of American troops arrived
To defend the Hindenburg Line from Allied tanks
To force Italy out of the war
questions.explain: Ludendorff gambled on a decisive breakthrough in spring 1918 before US forces could reinforce the Allies in strength.

questions.q: A soldier's diary reads: 'A greenish-yellow cloud drifted across no man's land; men began to choke and their eyes streamed.' Which weapon is being described?
questions.explain: The choking and greenish-yellow cloud describe a chlorine gas attack, a feature of trench warfare from 1915.

questions.q: A source notes that in September 1916 a new armoured vehicle crossed no man's land for the first time in the war. In which battle did this happen?
questions.explain: Tanks were used in combat for the first time at the Battle of the Somme in September 1916.

questions.q: A British newspaper in August 1914 declared: 'Britain cannot stand by while a small neutral nation is overrun.' Which event triggered Britain's declaration of war?
questions.explain: Germany's invasion of neutral Belgium broke the 1839 treaty guaranteeing its neutrality, prompting Britain to declare war on 4 August 1914.

questions.q: By autumn 1918 the German army was retreating after the Battle of Amiens, the naval blockade was causing severe food shortages, and Allied forces were advancing. Which conclusion best explains why Germany sought an armistice?
options: Germany's military position and home front had collapsed, making continued war impossible
Germany had won the war and wanted to dictate peace terms
Russia had rejoined the war on Germany's side
The USA had withdrawn its troops from Europe
questions.explain: Defeats in the Hundred Days Offensive, the blockade and unrest at home left Germany unable to continue, forcing it to seek an armistice.
